title: Dental Sealants Cost (2026): Price, Coverage and Benefits
h1: How Much Do Dental Sealants Cost, and Are They Worth It?
description: Dental sealants are thin coatings on back teeth that prevent cavities. What they cost, insurance coverage, who needs them and how they compare with fillings.
meta_keywords: dental sealants cost, cost of sealants, tooth sealant price, are dental sealants worth it
quick_answer: Dental sealants are thin plastic coatings painted onto the chewing surfaces of back teeth to keep out food and bacteria. No reliable national average price for sealants is published in our sources, but sealants are a quick preventive treatment priced per tooth and typically cost much less than a filling, which runs $165 to $530 for a composite on a back tooth without insurance (Delta Dental).
key_takeaways: Sealants protect the grooves of molars and premolars from decay.
They are priced per tooth and are quick, painless and preventive.
A filling for a back-tooth cavity costs $165 to $530 without insurance (Delta Dental).
Many plans cover sealants for children, often with age and frequency limits.
Sealants can last several years and can be repaired or reapplied.

sections.html:
Dental sealants are thin, protective coatings made of a resin material that a dentist or hygienist paints into the deep pits and grooves on the chewing surfaces of back teeth. These grooves are hard to clean with a toothbrush and are where most cavities in children and teens begin.

Once applied, the sealant hardens and forms a smooth barrier that keeps food and bacteria out of the grooves. Sealants are clear, white or slightly tinted and are not visible when you smile. The Cleveland Clinic's cavity guide explains why these grooves are so prone to decay.

sections.h2: How much do dental sealants cost?
sections.html:
Dental sealants are priced per tooth, and our sources do not publish a reliable national average for them. Prices vary by practice and region, and many offices set a modest fee per tooth because the procedure is quick and uses little material.

For context, a cavity in the same tooth would need a filling. Delta Dental lists a composite filling on a back tooth at $165 to $530 without insurance, and CareCredit reports averages of $226 for a composite and $139 for an amalgam filling. Ask your dentist for the sealant fee per tooth before treatment. See how much a filling costs.

Dental sealants are most often recommended for children and teenagers, ideally soon after the permanent molars come in, around ages 6 and 12. Sealing teeth early protects them during the years when cavity risk is highest.

Adults can also benefit from sealants if they have deep grooves without decay or fillings, a history of cavities, or a dry mouth. Your dentist will recommend sealants based on your cavity risk and the shape of your teeth.

Sealants are applied in a quick, painless procedure that usually takes a few minutes per tooth and needs no numbing or drilling.

  1. The tooth is cleaned and dried.
  2. A mild etching gel roughens the surface slightly so the sealant bonds.
  3. The tooth is rinsed and dried again.
  4. The sealant liquid is painted into the grooves.
  5. A curing light hardens the sealant.
  6. The dentist checks the bite and smooths any high spots.

You can eat and drink normally right afterward.

Many dental insurance plans cover sealants for children, often on permanent molars and up to a certain age, and sometimes only once every few years per tooth. Adult sealants are covered less often.

Coverage percentages vary; some plans treat sealants as preventive, others as basic care. Delta Dental's coverage guide explains how plan categories work. Check your plan's age and frequency limits. Medicaid and CHIP commonly cover sealants for eligible children. See tooth filling cost with insurance for comparison.

sections.h2: Are dental sealants worth the cost?
sections.html:
Dental sealants are often worth the cost because they are inexpensive per tooth, quick and painless, and can prevent cavities that would otherwise need fillings. A single avoided filling can cost more than sealing several teeth.

Sealants work best combined with good habits: brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, cleaning between teeth, limiting sugary snacks and drinks, and regular check-ups.

Sealants can last several years, and many last much longer. Chewing forces gradually wear them, and they can chip or come off, especially on teeth that take heavy biting.

Your dentist checks sealants at regular visits and can repair or reapply them when needed. Avoid chewing ice and hard candy, which can crack sealants.

sections.h2: How do sealants compare with fillings?
sections.html:
Sealants and fillings serve different purposes. Sealants prevent decay on healthy teeth; fillings repair teeth that already have cavities. A sealant requires no drilling, while a filling involves removing decay.

When a groove shows very early decay limited to the enamel, some dentists place a sealant or a small preventive resin restoration instead of a full filling. Your dentist decides based on X-rays and examination. See cavity filling and tooth filling cost without insurance.

Dental sealants are considered safe and have been used for decades. Some people ask about BPA in dental resins; the amounts involved are very small and short-lived. If you have concerns, ask your dentist which sealant material they use.

sections.h2: Why are sealants especially important for children?
sections.html:
Sealants are especially important for children because the deep grooves on newly erupted molars are difficult for young children to clean, and new enamel is more vulnerable to decay. Many cavities in children start in these grooves, which is why dentists often recommend sealing permanent molars soon after they come in.

Sealing teeth early can prevent fillings that would otherwise be needed during childhood and adolescence. Combined with fluoride, regular check-ups and limits on sugary snacks and drinks, sealants are one of the most effective ways to keep children's teeth cavity-free. School-based sealant programs in some areas also offer sealants to children at low or no cost.

Sealants need little maintenance beyond normal brushing, cleaning between teeth and regular dental check-ups. At each visit, the dentist or hygienist checks whether the sealants are intact and whether any edges have worn or chipped.

Worn areas can be touched up quickly by adding a little more sealant material. Because bacteria can collect under a damaged sealant, it is important not to skip check-ups. If you notice a rough spot or a piece missing, mention it at your next visit.

sections.h2: What should you ask your dentist about sealants?
sections.html: Ask your dentist which teeth would benefit from sealants, what the fee is per tooth, whether your insurance covers them, and how often they will be checked or replaced.

faq.q: How much do dental sealants cost?
faq.a: Dental sealants are priced per tooth, and our sources do not publish a reliable national average. They typically cost much less than a filling, which Delta Dental lists at $165 to $530 for a composite on a back tooth without insurance. Ask your dentist for the per-tooth fee.

faq.q: Are dental sealants covered by insurance?
faq.a: Many dental plans cover sealants for children, usually on permanent molars and up to a certain age, with frequency limits. Adult sealants are covered less often. Medicaid and CHIP commonly cover sealants for eligible children.

Adults can benefit from sealants if they have deep grooves without decay or fillings, a history of cavities or a dry mouth. Sealants are most commonly recommended for children and teens, but your dentist may suggest them at any age.

faq.q: How long do dental sealants last?
faq.a: Dental sealants can last several years or longer. They gradually wear from chewing and may chip, so dentists check them at regular visits and repair or reapply them when needed.
Sealants do not hurt. They are painted onto the tooth without drilling or numbing and hardened with a light, usually taking a few minutes per tooth.
